# Reference compression vectors (independent encoders)

Generated on ARM64 Kali (2026-10-29) with the REFERENCE compressors, not with rust-deobf's own test
encoder, so the decoders in scripts/decompress.py are checked against independent ground truth.

| file | encoder |
|---|---|
| `<name>.l1.blz`, `<name>.l10.blz` | BriefLZ, raw (headerless) stream: `blz_pack_level(src, dst, n, workmem, 1 / 10)` from jibsen/brieflz @ ad89acf (`src/brieflz.c`), via a 15-line driver (`rawblz.c`) |
| `text.blzpack` | `blzpack -9` (jibsen/brieflz example tool, same commit): blzpack container |
| `<name>.apl` | `apultra` v1.4.8 (emmanuel-marty/apultra @ 8f34005): raw aPLib-compatible stream |

Plaintexts (`<name>.plain`), all benign: `text` = the first 3000 bytes of this repo's README;
`config` = a neutral config-style text (`.example` host, RFC 5737 doc IP); `code` = the first 9000
bytes of tests/fixtures/vm/benign_rust_std.x64; `runs` = repeated patterns; `random` = 2048 seeded
random bytes (incompressible: the stream expands — the decoder must still be exact, and the
pipeline must NOT accept it without evidence).

`lz4_flex_0.11.6.json`: real lz4_flex 0.11.6 output (crates.io) from the generator in
`lz4_flex_gen/` (built with cargo / rustc 1.97 on x86-64 Linux, 2026-10-29): `block::compress`,
`block::compress_prepend_size`, the default `FrameEncoder`, and a `FrameEncoder` with content +
block checksums, content size and linked blocks. Plaintexts are regenerated by
tests/test_decompress.py (`_lz4_flex_plain`, same recipe as `main.rs`) and pinned by sha256.
